metadata.title: Why Is Palantir Stock Falling Today

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) shares fell about 4% on Thursday, extending losses as investors pulled back from richly valued enterprise software stocks amid broader market weakness and renewed geopolitical tensions.
The decline in Palantir came as concerns over the collapse of a U.S.-Iran truce weighed on risk sentiment, pushing major U.S. indexes lower. Investors also rotated away from high-valuation software companies, pressuring several artificial intelligence and enterprise technology names.
Other software companies moved lower alongside Palantir, including Salesforce (CRM), Oracle (NYSE:ORCL), and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW). The sector-wide retreat contrasted with Palantir's recent strategic initiatives, including expanding its AI capabilities through integration of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) Nemotron models and its collaboration with SNP SE, though those developments did little to offset broader market pressure.
Despite the selloff, the pullback appeared driven by macroeconomic and valuation concerns rather than company-specific news. Palantir has previously reported strong revenue growth and continues to expand its AI offerings, but investor sentiment remained tied to changing risk appetite across the technology sector.
